chapter_title: [Concerning the Five] War[s that the] Sons of [Li]ght waged with the Sons] of Darkness.
chapter_note: The oldest teaching layer is strongly dominant. This chapter preserves a systematic five-fold enumeration mapping five cosmic wars to five principal divinities (First Man, Living Spirit, Third Ambassador, Jesus the Splendour, Counsel of Life). The structure is complete and self-contained. Teaching purity is very high (0.842) with minimal editorial fatigue (0.09). The only significant editorial intrusions are: (1) the dialogue frame formula in ¶1, (2) a Gospel citation appended to the first war in ¶2 ('As the saviour has said...'), and (3) a beatitude/exhortation closure in ¶¶8-9. The five-fold enumeration with its systematic cosmic agents, cosmic actions, and cosmic outcomes is classic substrate. Heavy lacunae throughout (especially ¶¶4-5, 7) but the preserved skeleton is clearly correspondential-cosmological.

paragraphs.core_text: The sons of light waged five wars against the sons of darkness. The sons of light humiliated the sons of darkness in them all.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed opening dialogue frame formula 'Then the enlightener speaks:' — standard editorial attribution.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The thesis statement — five wars, sons of light vs. sons of darkness — defines the entire teaching structure. This is a substantive cosmological proposition, not a frame formula. The dialogue attribution wrapping it is clearly editorial.

paragraphs.core_text: The first war is that of the First living Man, which he waged against the King of the realms of Darkness, and all the rulers that had come forth from the five worlds of [...]. He hunted them with his net, which is the living soul. He [...] in the snare and [...] the face of the [...] his virgin, the living fire [...] they did not find how to escape his net [...] he caught them like fish [...] the five counsels of the five elements [...]. He cut and dug out the root of the five trees, [...] root of the evil tree, like an axe.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed Gospel citation at end: 'As the saviour has said: Behold, the axe is put to the root of the evil tree, so that from this time it can not bear evil fruit.' This is a NT citation (cf. Matt 3:10/Luke 3:9) — an editorial act that enters via the Gospel, not the substrate teaching. The institutional score (2.21) likely flags this citation.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The substrate core is rich: First Man, King of the realms of Darkness, five worlds, living soul, living fire, five counsels, five elements, five trees — all systematic cosmic mappings. The fishing/net/snare imagery is correspondential (cosmos→cosmos). The 'root of the evil tree' image was apparently present in the substrate, and the editor attached the Gospel citation to it. The seam is sharp: the substrate says 'like an axe' and then the editor glosses 'As the saviour has said...'

paragraphs.core_text: The second war is that of the Living Spirit [...]. He has constructed the things and the worlds of light; he spread out the rulers and chained them in the middle [...] the stars in [...] the earths [...] them in the three vessels. For the rulers rebelled and were set against the Living Spirit. They wished to [...] since they knew and realised that he might bind and fetter them with a strong chain. Yet he, the Living Spirit, (appeared to them) with many aspects, with numerous [...], with many hands and great cruelties. He was revealed to them, he imprisoned them with much skill. Not one of them was able to save (himself), and he {...} [...]. Now, since he [...] he trapped them [...] ⟨p.59⟩ [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system: Living Spirit → cosmic construction → chaining rulers → three vessels → stars and earths. The narrative of the rulers' futile rebellion is systematic cosmological process — describing what happened in the cosmic drama, not pointing to contemporary reality. 'Three vessels' is technical cosmic vocabulary.

paragraphs.core_text: The third war is that of the Third Ambassador who has displayed his image [...] what is below [...] scooped [...] all light and the property [...] the ones that are consumed [...] the entire ruling-power [...] pride of the light [...] extending it [...]. A person comes, who is powerful [...]; he takes his riches [...], silver [...], his pride and wantonness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substrate. The Third Ambassador displaying his image to seduce the archons and draw out light — a core cosmological process. The parable element ('A person comes, who is powerful...') is not an external citation but a correspondential illustration embedded within the cosmic teaching itself — both sides stay in the system. Silver as cosmic correspondence recalls the metal-realm mappings of Ch.6.

paragraphs.core_text: This is what the ruling-power is like [...], all riches [...] as they travel [...] light [...]. He cleansed and purified it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substrate continuation of the third war. Highest substrate density in the chapter (18.18). Despite heavy lacunae, the preserved text maps cosmic process: ruling-power, light, cleansing/purification — all internal to the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth war is this that Jesus the glorious one waged against all the rebels who had rebelled above and below. When the light was purified from them by the image of the Third Ambassador, their chains loosened [...]. The glorious one in the fourth war; he came and brought [...] a rebellion of the entire ruling-power. He girded himself [...] all of it another time. He constructed the whole structure and he made [...] a great contest; he humiliated therein. [...] he fulfilled the will of the greatness, [he gave the] hope to Adam [...] to his light ship.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substrate, though 'Jesus the glorious one' raises a compositional question. In Manichaean cosmology, Jesus the Splendour (Iesous Ziwa) occupies a structural slot in the emanation hierarchy as a cosmic being. Here he fills the fourth position in a five-fold war enumeration — his role is cosmic (subduing rebellion above and below, constructing structure, giving hope to Adam, light ship). Both sides of all mappings are internal to the cosmic system. Whether 'Jesus' was in the original Persian substrate or is Mani's substitution for an earlier cosmic agent is uncertain, but the teaching structure — the systematic role — is clearly substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth war is this that the counsel of life [...] which is the summons and the obedience [...] great [...] and it placed [...] upon the [...] and the [...] ⟨p.60⟩ [...] of death, which [...] with it. And it was victorious over [...] for ever, and it gave the kingdom [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substrate. The fifth and final war completing the enumeration. 'The counsel of life' and 'the summons and the obedience' are technical cosmological entities — the Call and Answer pair that effects final redemption. Despite extreme lacunae, the preserved structure (eschatological victory over death, giving the kingdom) maps cosmic process. Highest substrate score (18.87) confirms.

Exhortation/devotional closure. The shift from specific cosmic agents (counsel of life, summons, obedience) to generic categories ('the good... the wicked') marks a layer boundary. 'For ever and ever' is a devotional formula. Exhortation score 23.08 — the only paragraph in the chapter with any exhortation vocabulary. Position is classic: devotional summary appended after the five-fold teaching is complete.

Classic exhortation closure. 'Blessed is every elect one who will...' is the beatitude formula diagnostic of the exhortation layer. 'Elect one' is institutional vocabulary. 'After the likeness of these five' explicitly connects the preceding cosmic teaching to community application. The five-war teaching is complete and self-contained without this paragraph.
